newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tanker for Iraqi oil docks in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Tanker for Iraqi oil docks in Turkey.

text.p: An oil tanker to load the first Iraqi crude to be exported through Turkey in six years docked in the southern Turkish port of Ceyhan about midday on Saturday, witnesses said.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is to attend a ceremony at Ceyhan on Monday to celebrate the resumption of the flow of oil under the U.N. "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq.
After clearance from U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali last Monday, oil began flowing to Ceyhan this week through a 986-km (613-mile) pipeline from the Iraqi oil city of Kirkuk.

An official at Ceyhan said the vessel would load 153,000 tonnes of oil, an operation that would take about 20 hours. He did not say when the loading would begin and said that it would first take 12 to 13 hours to evacuate ballast.
The 150,000-tonne tanker Gole arrived offshore near Ceyhan on the Mediterranean on Friday morning, according to an official from Turkey's state refiner Tupras.

The tanker is to transport the crude to Tupras' Aliaga refinery in the western city of Izmir. A Tupras spokeswoman said some of the oil bought by Tupras under the contract might also be transported to the company's Kirikkale refinery, connected by a 447-km (278-mile) pipeline to Ceyhan.

Iraq pumped an average 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil, or nearly two-thirds of its total oil exports, through the pipeline before the U.N. embargo imposed after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990. Sanctions on Baghdad remain in place.

Tupras this week said the U.N. had approved its contract with Iraq to buy 75,000 bpd under the U.N. deal which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of crude for the purpose of buying food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies.
Iraq will use $1.3 billion of the oil revenues for the purchases, with the remaining funds going to a U.N. Compensation Fund and operating expenses.
The U.N. said on Thursday it had so far approved five contracts under the deal, including Tupras and the U.S. firm Coastal Corp. Coastal is expected to take 65,000 bpd.
France's Elf Aquitaine, whose initial contract was not accepted due to a technical point, is expected to be among the three other approved contracts.
Industry sources in Japan say Mitsubishi Corp is due to sign a 40,000 bpd accord for Iraqi oil.
